source.title: Features have life history. And we should care
source.authors: P. Stecher; Sandro Radovanovi'c; Vlasta Sikimić; Reinhard Kahle

page_placements.theme: Feature persistence and drift across model updates

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE-based feature tracking to Pythia language models across training checkpoints and reports results on feature recovery and stability, rather than reproducing the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper tests SAE-recovered features and their stability in real language models, but does not test superposition in the sense of overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions under capacity pressure. It reports SAE settings and cited prior work that are not independent findings about the claim; those are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses top-k SAEs as a tool to track feature 'life histories' across Pythia training checkpoints. It reports results about its own constructs: persistence, containment hierarchy, joint-ablation load and firing-versus-decoder convergence. No result asks whether features are superposed, whether polysemanticity reflects capacity, or whether SAE features are canonical or complete units of a fixed model. Active-feature counts are SAE outputs set by its hyperparameters (k=32, 64× expansion, alive threshold), not evidence that sparse features exist. Feature turnover across checkpoints reflects a changing model, not instability of the dictionary for one model.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that about 50 persistent SAE features form a 'carrier scaffold' early in training (mostly by step 1k, ~1% of training). The scaffold carries disproportionate joint cross-layer ablation load, is predictable from step-1k firing patterns (AUC 0.80/0.83), and organises 64%/53% of active features by convergence. They propose a two-phase account: selection fixes firing identity early, then training calibrates decoder directions. Transplantation suggests decoder calibration accounts for most of the carriers' load. They flag the evidence as correlational and limited to two Pythia scales, one corpus and four layers per scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses independent top-k SAEs at training checkpoints, post-hoc activation-profile matching, containment graphs, and joint cross-layer ablation. It does not use the original toy-model superposition experiment or measure overlapping near-orthogonal feature directions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported carrier counts and early-commitment fraction vary with the persistence threshold: at Pythia-160M, the ≥5-snapshot criterion gives 43 carriers with 86% born by step 1k, and the ≥6-snapshot criterion gives 37 carriers with 100% born by step 1k. Outcomes also vary by layer, including the Pythia-160M L11 late-training substrate failure.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Pythia training, SAE features with broad firing at step 1k persist far more often than narrow ones (43% vs 0.6% at 160M; 38% vs 0.4% at 410M). Firing profiles converge by step 1k while decoder directions calibrate over the rest of training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-feature firing identity stabilises early in LM training while decoder directions keep changing; only a small broad-firing subset persists across training.

fits_no_version.finding: Jointly ablating persistent carriers costs more cross-entropy than count-matched non-persistent roots at both scales. Matched leaves cost near zero at 160M but +0.24 nats at 410M.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporally persistent SAE-feature populations carry more joint-ablation load than matched non-persistent populations.

fits_no_version.finding: At Pythia-160M L11 late in training, the SAE collapses to ~37 active features and loss recovery goes negative (−0.33). A 10× training budget does not fix it; the authors tie this to residual-stream rank collapse to ~13 dims.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Top-k SAEs can fail to find a sparse dictionary in layers whose activations collapse to low effective rank.

fits_no_version.finding: A containment hierarchy seeded by carriers reaches 64% (160M) and 53% (410M) of active features at convergence; organised features fire more narrowly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features organise into a firing-containment hierarchy seeded by early persistent features.

record.problems: The study covers only two Pythia scales, one training corpus, and four residual-stream layers per scale. The authors describe the evidence as correlational and note that it does not establish a causal formation mechanism. The feature-tracking results depend on SAE feature matching and thresholds; Pythia-160M L11 has a pronounced SAE substrate failure.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no feature-versus-dimension count, no sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No test that features are spread across neurons or that SAEs recover model features beyond the SAE's own output; SAE reconstruction quality is relegated to the appendix.
No test of completeness, canonicality, or stability of SAE features for a fixed model across SAE seeds or sizes. Seed replication is reported only as carrier counts (±12%).
All: no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4, and all reader labels dropped. SAEs are the study's instrument; its findings concern training dynamics of SAE features, not superposition or the canonicality of dictionary features. Treating cross-checkpoint feature death as evidence on V5 would conflate model change with dictionary instability. The seed-replication control (carrier counts vary ≤12%) and the L11 SAE failure come closest to V5/V4 but are reported as tool robustness, not as tests of the claim. The paper cites superposition work only for its SAE method.

versions.untested_parts: No test of more features than dimensions, overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry.
No test of polysemantic neurons, capacity competition between features, or dedicated dimensions for important features.
No test of polysemantic neurons arising through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
Tests SAE feature recovery in Pythia at four sampled layers per scale; does not test whether features are spread across neurons, or generalisation to other architectures, scales, or training corpora.

Tests temporal persistence of selected SAE features and distinguishes firing-pattern identity from decoder direction. Does not establish that SAE features are complete, canonical, or uniquely determined units of the model.
Uses individual SAE decoder columns but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features or test the dimensionality of the underlying features.

relation.reason: SAEs supply the feature representation used for the analysis; persistence and geometric change across model training checkpoints do not test canonicality or stability within a fixed model.

tranche.reason: The study uses SAE decompositions to investigate feature histories, containment, prediction and ablation load. Its results do not test any listed superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The qualitative convergence results concern persistent carriers. Appendix D's within-5% result concerns consecutive-checkpoint distances, whereas Fig. 3 compares each checkpoint with step 143k.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pythia-160M and Pythia-410M at step 143k, across the four instrumented layers
reader_labels.reason: SAEs yield thousands of active features in both models, and the measured containment hierarchy includes many active features (R1, R2, R7, R8).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The SAE substrate fails in this layer: active feature count falls from 612 at step 80k to 39 at step 120k and 37 at step 143k (R19).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Persistent carrier subset in Pythia-160M and Pythia-410M
reader_labels.reason: The study tracks 51 and 49 persistent carriers, respectively, and reports that many eventual carriers are present by step 1k with firing identity already largely settled (R3–R6, R15, R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Step-1k feature populations and decoder directions in both Pythia models
reader_labels.reason: Persistence is strongly selective by firing-entropy quartile, and decoder directions begin near-random at step 1k and calibrate later; the paper supports stability of firing identity for selected carriers, not universal feature stability (R11–R14, R17, R18).
